_is qui foris est_ (…) _is qui intus est_ – the one who is outside (…) the one who is inside. This is the classical passage about the “inner man” and the “outer man,” a terminology not received into the Vulgate. The expressions that came to be used in theology – _exterior homo_, _interior homo_ – come from this very passage’s words of the Vetus Latina. – Literature:
1951. Otto Hiltbrunner: Exterior homo. _Vigiliae Christianae_ 5: 55–60, esp. pp. 56–57.
1977. Hans Peter Rüger: Hieronymus, die Rabbinen und Paulus (2 Kor 4,16). _Zeitschrift für die neutestamentliche Wissenschaft_ 68: 132–137. Rabbinic parallels to Jerome’s comments on Koheleth 9:14–15.
